If you've been looking at investing but you don't know how to get started I got you. Today, I am going to be breaking down top investment apps for beginners in Nigeria. These platforms have made it easier and accessible for everyone, so whether you're a complete beginner or you're looking at leveling up your investments game then keep watching. Hi 👋 everyone, welcome back to my channel my name is Doyinsola Toye on this channel, I share tips on how to make, manage and multiply money. So, today I am going to be breaking down the top investment apps that is available for a beginner and someone who is looking at leveling up their investment game. So, if this looks like you then get a pen and a paper and start jotting things down. I am going to be talking about the top investment apps in no particular order No. 1 is Bamboo, with bamboo you can invest in US stocks, local stocks (Nigerian stocks), ETFs, fixed deposit in dollar and also invest in Treasury Bills perhaps you're wondering but I don't have a dorm account, you don't need to have a dorm account, a dollar account before you can invest in US stocks or ETFs. your naira is going to be converted to dollar at the prevailing exchange rates and then you can buy shares of Apple, Microsoft, Tesla, VOO ETF, VGT ETF and you can also do fractional shares So, let's say for example a share of Apple is going for $200 and you're saying oh I don't have up to $200 that I want to invest at once so even if it's $10 you have or if it's $5 or even if it is $1 that you have it allows you to buy the units of share based on the amount you have so that means instead of getting one unit you might be getting maybe 0.00000 something and when you continue to invest over time before you know it you are having 10 units, five units as the case may be so don't let the fact that oh this share is going for $200 or $500 I don't have it allows you to do fractional share investing so with your naira, you are able to invest in US stocks you are able to invest in ETFs, you can also buy Nigerian stocks on Bamboo you can do a fixed deposit in dollar on Bamboo and then you can also buy Treasury Bills on Bamboo it is user-friendly, easy to use you just need to download the app on the App Store or play Store register your details, your BVN is going to be required so you don't have anything to worry about. It is regulated by SEC So, what are you waiting for? No, wait watch the rest So, the next on the list is Cowrywise Cowrywise allows you to save and invest automatically right from the app on your phone with Cowrywise, you get interest on your savings much more than your traditional bank account is going to give you your bank is giving you maybe about 1 to 5% per annum but on Cowrywise you can get as high as 22% per annum there is a feature on Cowrywise that I love which is safe lock you can decide to lock your funds for a long period of time and then you get to enjoy higher interest right there is what we call duo savings you and your partner can decide to jointly save right that's like a joint account right on Cowrywise. You can also do a savings challenge perhaps you and your girlies, right your friends, your guy friends you want to go on a vacation and you want to save money right that is a good one to do perhaps instead of doing Ajo where interest is not coming in why not you and your friends come together, pull funds together right and then you get some little interest even if it's little don't despise small beginnings right so you and your friends can come together go on a saving challenge and do that. Another feature that I also love on Cowrywise, is AutoSave so no story of oh I forgot to save this month, you set up auto-save so that means you have to link your bank account or your card right to the Cowrywise app okay this time of the month I want you to deduct  or withdraw this X amount of money from my bank account and then it is saved on your Cowrywise wallet. Also, you can invest in naira or dollar mutual funds on Cowrywise so instead of going to Stanbic, ARM, FSDH, right on the Cowrywise app you have variety of mutual fund, money market fund that you can invest in, you can see their rates and you choose which one suits you the most and then there are different types of mutual fund, the Equity based, the moderate, the conservative that you can play around it is user-friendly, easy, just take your time, play around the app right. The next one is Piggyvest, Piggyvest is also a fintech platform like Cowrywise allows you to save automatically and just like Cowrywise you also have the auto-save option on Piggyvest This evening, I got a debit I'm like what's this debit for, I remember that I had even set up autosave so without of course you’ve given your consent from the beginning the money is deducted from your account and is saved in your Piggyvest wallet right there are different features on Piggyvest there's also the Safe Lock option on Piggyvest that gives you higher interest right and now you get your interest upfront there's also what we call flexi, it's like an emergency savings that allows you to withdraw up to four times a month without any charges. If you do more than 4 times that is when you will be charged right so perhaps in the next video I'm going to explain what emergency savings is all about there are also some investments that you can do on Piggyvest platform They have the Investify, Corporate debt note as well that opens up from time to time on Piggyvest right so you can download the app on the Play Store or App Store the next is Risevest yes with Risevest, you can invest in real estate yes in dollars you can invest in stocks, you can do fixed deposits and then you can save as well on Risevest but you're better off doing real estate investment or doing what's it called fixed investment rather than just saving because the interest that you get on the real estate or the fixed investment or the stock is much better off than just saving on Risevest and just like Bamboo, you don't need a dorm account right your naira is going to be converted to dollar at the prevailing exchange rate yeah it is going to be converted at the prevailing exchange rate on the platform. Also, on Piggyvest I forgot to mention that you can save in dollars on Piggyvest I remember that my first saving in dollars was on Piggyvest saving as low as 400 I was able to buy dollar right 400 and then the rate then was 8% per annum I was able to buy at 400, I bought at 500 I bought 600, 900, 1000+ and I was getting credited interest at the end of every month so with Risevest as well you can save in dollar, you can invest in real estate, you can invest in stocks, and then you can do fixed investment on Risevest. The next one is Trove, Trove is a platform that allows you to invest in US stocks, ETFs, and local stocks. With Trove, you can buy shares of Microsoft, Apple, Gt-bank  So, Trove allows you to invest in Nigerian stocks The next on the line is Afrinvest, Afrinvest, Afrinvestor, Afrinvest allows you to invest in local stocks so on Afrinvest, you can invest in Nigerian stocks, buy shares of Firstbank, Dangote, fidelity etc. Through Afrinvest, as well you can invest in the FGN savings bond but not on the app yeah so we have the Afrnvestor 2.0 app we have Afrinvest itself so if you want to invest in the FGN savings bond you have to send them an email but if you want to invest in local stocks you can use the app but you need to have what we call CSCS number and CHN number I have a video on how to get your CSCS number and your CHN number especially for people who want to go in the line of investing in FGN savings bond. Afrinvest also have an app called Optimus you can save on Optimus, you can invest in US stocks on Optimus, and you can buy mutual fund on Optimus So, the Optimus app is also by Afrinvest so you have Afrinvestor 2.0 which allows you invest in local stocks and then you have Optimus that allows you to save in naira, you can also save in dollar, allows you to invest in US stocks and buy ETFs and also allow you to invest in mutual fund and equity fund on the Optimus app. The next is Chaka right  Chaka/Yochaa, they are also like Trove that allows you to invest in US stocks and allow you to invest in local stock also apps like Fair Money Renmoney and the likes allows you to save and get as much as possible. So, you see like you literally have no excuse for not starting your investment journey because these are apps that are available at your finger tips. So, if you have a smartphone with internet go to Playstore and App store you can also check out their website to read more on them, the different regulations with SEC, CBN and all the likes that they have and then you go ahead to start investing right away and you know like I usually say that you don't need millions of naira before you start investing with your 5,000 naira, you can begin your investment journey Like I mention that with $1, $5, $10 you can start investing in US stocks, in ETFs on Bamboo or Trove as the case may be. So, there you go top investment apps that is available for you to start investing I want to hear from you in the comment section which one do you want to start researching on this week and start making plans to start investing with them or saving with them literally you have no excuse still saving in your traditional bank account imagine a 1 to 5% per annum compared to 22, getting free money without stress just because you are saving or just because you are investing right. Another app I forgot to mention is the FSDH app. The FSDH app allows you to invest in mutual fund I personally do FSDH mutual fund so you are able to invest in mutual fund on the FSDH app right. So, you see there are tons of app and this is not get rich quick scheme anything these apps, a number of them are regulated by SEC and CBN so you have nothing to worry about majority or let me say all of this app is going to request for your BVN so you have nothing to worry about and please ensure that you do your proper due diligence as well. If you think that your heart or whatever is not going with any of the app it's okay, it's not compulsory that you download all the apps on your account and yeah start investing on all of them, no, it is not compulsory that you have all the apps. Do your research, do your due diligence and select the ones that aligns with your financial goal right and start investing with them. So, there you have it, the top investment apps if you think I forgot anyone please drop it in the comment section and I'm going to say one or two things about it. If you enjoyed this video, you found it educative, interesting, and inspiring don't forget to like, share, follow for more tips on building wealth and I will see you in my next video cheers.
